canonical.title: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
canonical.sourceFilePath: 14. Dynamic Programming/9. DP on Squares/02. Count square submatrices.cpp

narrative.title: The Turf Mosaic Inventory
narrative.scenario: A stadium groundskeeper maps a grass grid where 1 marks healthy turf and 0 marks worn patches. Maintenance orders are sized in square sections, and any all-healthy square — of any size, anywhere — can be turfed in one work order. The scheduler counts every all-ones square block in the grid to size the season's workload.
narrative.inputFormat: An m x n binary matrix matrix of 0s and 1s.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the number of square submatrices (of all sizes) consisting entirely of 1s.

testCases.explanation: Ten 1x1 squares, four 2x2 squares, and one 3x3 square — 15 total.

hintLevels: Level 1: Same cell recurrence as maximal square — but each cell's value is itself a count contribution.
Level 2: side[i][j] counts squares of every size whose bottom-right corner lands at (i, j); sum them all.
Level 3: A side-s value at a corner implies exactly s new squares ending there — one of each size up to s.
